$comment: Shared policy, versioned so every machine enforces the same rules.
Machine-specific overrides live outside this repository, in the overlay that
`secure-npm edit-policy` opens; it is shallow-merged on top of this file.
Editing this file changes nothing until `node install.mjs` redeploys it.
$allowedGitSourcesComment: Exception list for git dependencies, consulted whenever allowExoticSources
is false. Entries are repositories written as host/owner/repo, matched at any
depth against the normalised form of every git specifier and every lockfile
https://github.com/owner/repo all reduce to github.com/owner/repo. A '*' stands
for exactly one path segment, so host/owner/* covers a whole organisation and
nothing beyond it. Refused sources print the exact string to add here.
Whitelisting a repository also exempts it from the release-age check: a commit
has no registry publish date, and the version it declares is not the registry's.
$trustPolicyComment: pnpm-only, and enforced natively by pnpm: refuses a version published with
weaker guarantees (provenance, trusted publisher) than an earlier one, which
is what a stolen publish token looks like. The comparison is by publish date
rather than semver, so a backport onto an old branch trips it; the ignore-after
window keeps the check on the recent releases where the risk actually is.
$compromisedPackagesComment: Curated list of npm packages that are known to be malicious, maintained by
DataDog. Names on it are refused at any depth, on both managers, and
'secure-npm validate' audits an existing tree against the same list.
The list is cached, and refreshed once it is older than the refresh window.
When a refresh fails the cached copy is used and announced, up to the
max-stale window; past that an install is refused rather than run
unchecked. Setting the source to "" switches the check off entirely.
